reasoning_traces.think:
The feed inventory primitive establishes a baseline for event novelty using a Bayesian update over a known seen-index. It ensures that only truly new information enters the system, preventing redundancy and maintaining signal-to-noise ratios. The breakeven conversion rate primitive introduces a decision-theoretic lens into situational reasoning, enabling GSE to assess whether a strategic move is robust under uncertainty. The historical data aggregation primitive provides the empirical foundation for both systems, grounding predictions in large-scale, time-series data. Together, these primitives form a triadic logic: novelty detection → strategic evaluation → empirical grounding. Each operator has a clear failure mode—feed duplication leads to false positives, incorrect breakeven thresholds lead to suboptimal decisions, and biased historical data undermines model validity.
